evidence.source: Academia Sinica, Chinese Character Database (中央研究院漢字構形資料庫)
evidence.field: 字形演變; character record 馬, U+99AC
evidence.text: The page lists oracle-bone, bronze (including 集成02594), Chu slip and silk, small-seal, and Shuowen forms. Its account describes 馬 as depicting the whole animal, emphasizing the eye, mane, body, and long tail. It does not assign semantic or phonetic roles to subcomponents.
evidence.title: 漢字「馬」：字形演變

search_audit.query: 馬 oracle bone bronze inscription pictograph Academia Sinica Xiaoxuetang 馬 字形
search_audit.outcome: Inspected the Academia Sinica character-specific evolution record. It supports a whole-animal pictograph analysis and lists historical script categories, but does not provide a dated earliest individual inscription in inspected text.

search_audit.query: Wikimedia Commons 馬 oracle bone script bronze inscription glyph image
search_audit.outcome: Inspected candidate image description pages and Commons reuse guidance. Oracle and Western Zhou bronze modern SVG redrawings have direct original file URLs and stated rights. Attempts to open raw SVG through the web tool failed because it does not render SVG; this does not alter the source-page identity or rights claims.

search_audit.query: open candidate seal script 馬 Wikimedia Commons file page for graphic development
search_audit.outcome: Inspected candidate seal-script file page; no additional glyph selected because oracle and Western Zhou bronze examples better illustrate the supported pictographic features and early form range.

gaps: No date for the earliest individual 馬 inscription or earliest lexical use was confirmed in the inspected character-specific primary page. The page lists oracle-bone forms but its textual summary does not date them.
No dated attestations for later sense extensions or surname usage were researched in this image-provenance-focused pass; dictionary gloss order is not used to infer chronology.

The evidence supports 馬 as a whole-animal pictograph. No separate semantic or phonetic subcomponents are proposed; the Shuowen component account is historical testimony, not independent confirmation of the exact earliest graphic details.
The dossier's claim that simplified 马 follows a cursive form was not rechecked in this invocation. No simplification image is proposed, and no specific derivational chronology is inferred.

Direct SVG image endpoints were rejected by the browser as unsupported content type. Their file description pages, direct URLs, descriptions, and reuse statements were inspected; no claim of visual inspection is made.

items.period: Shang (as labeled by the image source; specific inscription date not given)
items.caption: A modern vector redraw of 馬 in Shang oracle-bone script style. The form is presented as a whole-animal pictograph.
items.alt: Black line drawing of an early 馬 graph, with a prominent head and eye, body, mane or tail strokes, and legs.
items.selection_reason: Shows an early form corresponding to the paleographic database’s whole-animal account; file page names the Sinica database as a source.
items.rights: Public domain representation of ancient script according to the Commons file description; modern redraw, not an artifact photograph.

items.period: Mid-Western Zhou (source associates Sinica form 33.E88A with 彔伯⿹戈冬簋蓋)
items.caption: A modern vector redraw of a Western Zhou bronze-script 馬 form associated by the source page with a mid-Western Zhou vessel inscription.
items.alt: Black line drawing of 馬 in a bronze-script style, with a large eye, mane, body, tail, and legs rendered as linear strokes.
items.selection_reason: Pairs an oracle-style example with a historical bronze-style stage listed in the paleographic source; gives more specific period context through the file-page vessel note.
items.rights: The file description says the Sinica-sourced image is CC0 1.0; it also contains a separate project permission note. This is a modern vector redraw, not a photograph of the vessel.

limitations.text: The web tool rejected the direct SVG endpoints as unsupported content type, so the glyph pixels were not visually inspected in this research stage. File pages identify the candidates, scripts, direct original URLs, and rights; visual review remains for the downstream image inspector.

The Commons bronze file page supplies a vessel association and approximate mid-Western Zhou period for its linked Sinica example, while the Academia Sinica evolution page lists bronze forms and catalogue references without textual dating in the inspected lines. The SVG should be treated as a sourced modern rendering, not an artifact image.
